# Mid-Sprint Check-in: @arjunsb26

## Question 1: What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?

My main work so far is #14, the milestone burndown chart, which was carried over from Sprint 1. PR #77 merged on 10-09. The milestone page now draws a burndown with an ideal line and a projected finish date. It marks where scope was added or removed, and hovering over a day lists the items that changed on it. A checkbox, saved in the URL, adds pull requests to the chart. The history is rebuilt from timeline comments, so it needed no migration. The PR has Go unit, integration, Vitest and e2e tests. After review I fixed stale responses when the toggle is clicked quickly, and a projection that was measured from the wrong day.

What remains is all of my Sprint 2 load. I have no issues on the Sprint 2 milestone yet. I need to pick two medium issues, write their specs with a design decision, get them peer-reviewed, and then implement them with Tech Debt sections. I also need to draw the UML diagrams for one of them, file my AI logs, and review a teammate's PR.

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

I learned that a permission check on a route doesn't always mean the data behind it is safe to show. The milestone pages let in anyone who can read issues *or* pull requests, so adding my chart endpoint to the same route group was not enough. A viewer who could read issues but not pull requests would still have seen pull request titles in the chart. The server now counts and lists a kind only if the viewer can read it, and two integration tests turn off each unit and check that nothing leaks. I confirmed that both tests fail when the check is removed, because a test that never fails proves nothing.

I also learned that Gitea's timeline comments work as an event log. Replaying them lets you rebuild the past without storing daily snapshots, but the replay has to end on the database's current state. Otherwise the chart can disagree with the progress bar right above it.

## Question 3: What is one thing you would do differently?

I would check my work against the acceptance criteria before calling it done, not after. When I asked the AI whether #14 was complete, it found that the first version had missed three criteria: the scope markers, the hover details and the pull request toggle. Adding them late meant a second round of commits, more tests and another merge from main. If I had kept the criteria list open as a checklist while I worked, I would have caught those gaps on the first day.

I would also start my Sprint 2 issues sooner. Finishing #14 took the first part of the sprint, and I put off choosing new issues until it merged. That leaves the spec reviews, which depend on teammates' turnaround, crowded into the second week. Writing the specs while #14 was in review would have kept both moving at once.---

### User Story

As a keyboard or screen reader user managing a repository, I want the "…" menus on workflow runs, workflows, project columns and package cleanup rules to be operable from the keyboard, so that I can cancel a run, disable a workflow or edit a column without a mouse.

### User Scenario

A maintainer using a screen reader opens the Actions tab. They Tab to a running job's "…" button and hear "More operations, menu button, collapsed". They press Enter, arrow to "Cancel" and press Enter, and the run is cancelled. They open the workflow's "…" menu, where "Disable workflow" is announced as "dimmed" because the workflow is required, so pressing Enter on it does nothing. On a project board they open a column's "…" menu and choose "Edit", and the edit dialog opens.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the Actions tab, when it renders, then the workflow "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/list.tmpl`) and every run row's "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl`) are `<aria-menu>` elements with no `ui dropdown` class, and each trigger is named "More operations".
- [ ] AC2: Given a project board and a user with write access, when it renders, then each column's "…" menu (`templates/projects/view.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`. Edit opens the column modal, and "Set as default" and "Delete" show their confirmation dialogs, by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC3: Given a package cleanup rule list, when it renders, then each rule's "…" menu (`templates/package/shared/cleanup_rules/list.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`, and "Edit" and "Preview" navigate.
- [ ] AC4: Given a menu item with the `disabled` class, when the menu is open, then the item has `aria-disabled="true"`, arrow keys still reach it, and Enter, Space or a click on it does nothing and leaves the menu open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a required workflow, when its "…" menu is opened, then "Disable workflow" is disabled as in AC4. For a workflow that isn't required, it sends the same enable/disable request as today.
- [ ] AC6: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, Home/End and the arrows move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC7: Given a project board, when a column's "…" menu is opened or used by keyboard, then the column is not picked up or moved by the board's drag-and-drop. The menu sits inside `.project-column-header`, which `web_src/js/features/repo-projects.ts` uses as the Sortable drag handle.
- [ ] AC8: A Vitest test in `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.test.ts` covers AC4. Playwright tests cover cancelling a run and opening a column's Edit dialog by keyboard. The existing suites still pass.

### Out of Scope

- The "Create new runner" menu (`templates/shared/actions/runner_list.tmpl`): it holds a text input and a copy button, so it is a popup, not a menu.
- The Actions page filter menus (actor, status, branch): they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- The run page's own re-run menu in `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue`.

### Open Questions

- Should a disabled item also say *why* it is disabled (for example "required by organisation settings")? (Proposed: not in this issue. Today the menu shows no reason either.)
- Should the run row menus use `placement="bottom-end"`, since they sit at the right edge of each row?

### Design Decision

### Decision 1: which component to move to
**Decision:** Rebuild the four menus as `<aria-menu>` and keep every item's `link-action`, `show-modal` and `data-modal-confirm` attributes, as #62 did for the comment menu.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Keep the Fomantic dropdowns and extend the ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`.
- (b) Move only the Actions menus and leave Projects and Packages for later.

**Rationale:** (a) can't fix the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md`, and upstream is removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849). (b) would leave the same "…" menu working two different ways depending on the page. All four share one markup shape and the delegated `link-action`/`show-modal` handlers, so the extra two cost little.

**Consequences:** Easier: every "…" row menu outside the issue sidebar behaves the same, and `dropdown.ts` handles four fewer menu types. Harder: a run list can render many `<aria-menu>` elements per page, each with its own listeners. That's fine at 20–50 rows, but if the list ever grows unpaginated, a single delegated menu would scale better.

### Decision 2: how disabled items work
**Decision:** Teach `<aria-menu>` to mark `.item.disabled` children `aria-disabled="true"` in `updateItemRoles`. They stay focusable but don't activate, and the menu stays open on Enter, Space or click.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Leave disabled items out of the menu when the workflow is required.
- (b) Skip disabled items when moving with the arrow keys.

**Rationale:** The WAI-ARIA menu pattern keeps disabled items focusable so screen reader users learn the option exists. (a) hides that, and it changes what sighted users see. (b) matches neither the APG nor native OS menus, and a user who can only reach an item by pointer would never hear about it.

**Consequences:** Easier: any later menu with a disabled item works without extra code. Harder: this changes the shared component, so the navbar and comment menus from #62 must be re-checked. The existing `aria-menu.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` cover them.

### Scope

type BurndownStatus string

const (
	BurndownEmpty            BurndownStatus = "empty"             // nothing has ever been in the milestone
	BurndownDone             BurndownStatus = "done"              // every item in it is closed
	BurndownClosed           BurndownStatus = "closed"            // the milestone was closed with items still open
	BurndownProjected        BurndownStatus = "projected"         // a finish date could be extrapolated
	BurndownNotBurning       BurndownStatus = "not_burning"       // remaining work has not fallen over the window
	BurndownInsufficientData BurndownStatus = "insufficient_data" // too few days of history to extrapolate
)

const (
	burndownWindowDays     = 14  // the projection extrapolates the net burn rate over at most this many days
	burndownMinHistoryDays = 2   // a rate over fewer days is noise, not a trend
	burndownHorizonDays    = 365 // a due date further out than this past the chart is not drawn
)

// BurndownPoint is the state of a milestone at the end of one day.
func GetMilestoneBurndown(ctx context.Context, m *issues_model.Milestone, opts BurndownOptions) (*MilestoneBurndown, error) {
	scopeEvents, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneScopeEvents(ctx, m.RepoID, m.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	movedIDs := make([]int64, 0, len(scopeEvents))
	for _, e := range scopeEvents {
		movedIDs = append(movedIDs, e.IssueID)
	}
	slices.Sort(movedIDs)
	items, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneItems(ctx, m.RepoID, m.ID, slices.Compact(movedIDs))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// a left-out kind is not counted and not listed, so a viewer never learns of items they cannot read
	items = slices.DeleteFunc(items, func(item issues_model.MilestoneItem) bool {
		return item.IsPull && !opts.Pulls || !item.IsPull && !opts.Issues
	})

	itemIDs := make([]int64, 0, len(items))
	for _, item := range items {
		itemIDs = append(itemIDs, item.ID)
	}
	stateEvents, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneStateEvents(ctx, itemIDs)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return CalcMilestoneBurndown(m, items, append(scopeEvents, stateEvents...), time.Now(), setting.DefaultUILocation), nil
}

## User Story

As a maintainer tracking several milestones, I want the milestones list to show each open milestone's projected finish, so that I can see which milestones are slipping without opening each burndown chart (#14).

## User Scenario

A maintainer opens a repository's Milestones tab, where three milestones are open. Under "Sprint 3" they see "Projected Nov 12 · 4 days late" in red next to the due date. "Docs refresh" reads "Projected Nov 2 · on track". "Backlog" has no due date, and reads "Projected Dec 1". A fourth milestone, opened yesterday, shows nothing because there isn't enough history yet. They click "Sprint 3", and its burndown chart shows the same Nov 12 projection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open milestone with a due date whose burndown status is `projected`, when the Milestones tab renders, then its row shows the projected finish date and either "N days late" in red (projected after the due date) or "on track" (on or before it).
- [ ] AC2: Given an open milestone with no due date whose status is `projected`, when the list renders, then its row shows the projected finish date and no late or on-track label.
- [ ] AC3: Given an open milestone whose status is `not_burning`, when the list renders, then its row shows "Not burning down" in the warning colour. A status of `empty`, `insufficient_data` or `done` shows nothing new.
- [ ] AC4: Given a closed milestone, when the closed tab renders, then its row shows no projection.
- [ ] AC5: Given any open milestone, when the list renders, then the projected date and day count match those on that milestone's own page with the chart's default kind (issues, or pull requests for a viewer who can read only pull requests).
- [ ] AC6: Given a viewer who can read issues but not pull requests (or the reverse), when the list renders, then the projection counts only the kind they can read, as the chart does.
- [ ] AC7: A Go unit test covers the status-to-label mapping (late, on track, no due date, not burning, nothing). An integration test covers the list page for AC1, AC4 and AC6, and the existing burndown tests still pass.

## Out of Scope

- Sorting or filtering the list by projected finish.
- The cross-repository milestones dashboard (`/milestones`).
- An "include pull requests" toggle on the list: the list uses the chart's default kind.
- Caching or storing projections. See Decision 1.

## Open Questions

- Should "on track" have a colour (green), or stay muted so that only late milestones stand out? (Proposed: muted.)
- Should the list compute projections only for open milestones on the current page? (Proposed: yes, so the cost is bounded by the page size.)

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: where the projection is computed

**Decision:** Compute it on the server in the `Milestones` handler, calling the existing `issue.GetMilestoneBurndown` for each open milestone on the current page, and render it in `templates/repo/issue/milestones.tmpl`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Fetch each row's projection in the browser from the existing `/milestone/{id}/burndown` JSON endpoint.
- (b) Store the projected finish in a new `milestone` column, recomputed whenever an issue opens, closes or changes milestone.

**Rationale:** (a) costs one HTTP request per row, makes the rows shift as results arrive, and shows nothing without JavaScript. (b) needs a migration and hooks on every issue state and milestone change, and a stored projection goes stale as days pass with no events, because the burn rate is measured over a time window. Server-side reuse keeps a single source of truth, so AC5 holds by construction.

**Consequences:** Easier: no new endpoint, migration or JavaScript, and the list can never disagree with the chart. Harder: each open milestone on the page costs a few queries (scope events, items, state events). That is bounded by the page size, but a repository with long milestone histories may load the list more slowly. If it does, a batched query or a cache is the follow-up.

### Decision 2: what the row shows

**Decision:** Show a text label: the projected date, plus "N days late" or "on track" when there is a due date.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A small sparkline of the burndown in each row.
- (b) An on/off-track badge from comparing remaining work to the ideal line today.

**Rationale:** (a) is unreadable at row size, adds a chart library to the list page, and gives a screen reader nothing useful without extra text. (b) can say "off track" while the projection says it will finish on time, because the ideal line and the projection measure different things. The chart page would then contradict the list.

**Consequences:** Easier: the label is plain text, so it's accessible and testable with an HTML assertion. Harder: the list doesn't show the trend's shape, so users open the milestone for that.

## Scope

      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);

  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
  updateItemRoles() {
    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
      } else {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
      }
    }
  }

  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys

> ### Decision 3: keeping the column menu out of drag-and-drop (@arjunsb26)
>
> **Decision:** Add `filter: 'aria-menu'` with `preventOnFilter: false` to the column Sortable in `web_src/js/features/repo-projects.ts`, so a press that starts on the menu never begins a drag.

> **Alternatives Considered:**
> - (a) Stop the menu's pointer and keyboard events from propagating, inside `<aria-menu>`.
> - (b) Move the menu out of `.project-column-header`.
>
> **Rationale:** (a) puts board-specific code in the shared component, and it can also block the delegated `link-action`/`show-modal` handlers that rely on events bubbling. (b) changes the column header's layout and moves the menu away from where users expect it. Sortable's `filter` option is meant for exactly this, and it is a one-line change in the one file that owns the board.
>
> **Consequences:** Easier: `<aria-menu>` stays generic. Harder: any later interactive control in the column header needs adding to the filter too.

```text
import {generateElemId, hideElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Optional host attributes, read only by CSS: placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing, floating
// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
window.customElements.define('aria-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
  trigger!: HTMLElement;
  popup!: HTMLElement;
  inited = false;

  connectedCallback() {
    // in <head>-loaded components, the children are not parsed yet while the page is still loading
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init, {once: true});
    } else {
      this.init();
    }
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    document.removeEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init);
    if (this.inited) this.close(false); // also removes the outside click listener
  }

  init = () => {
    if (this.inited) return;
    const popup = this.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .menu');
    const trigger = Array.from(this.children).find((el) => el !== popup) as HTMLElement | undefined;
    if (!popup || !trigger) return;
    this.inited = true;
    this.popup = popup;
    this.trigger = trigger;

    if (trigger.tagName !== 'BUTTON') {
      trigger.setAttribute('role', 'button');
      trigger.tabIndex = 0;
    }
    if (!popup.id) popup.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-popup-');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', popup.id);
    popup.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    if (!popup.hasAttribute('aria-label') && !popup.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')) {
      if (!trigger.id) trigger.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-trigger-');
      popup.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', trigger.id); // keeps the menu's name once focus is on an item
    }
    hideElem(popup);
    this.updateItemRoles();

    trigger.addEventListener('click', () => this.isOpen() ? this.close(true) : this.open('first'));
    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', this.onTriggerKeyDown);
    trigger.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('keydown', this.onPopupKeyDown);
    popup.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);
    });
  };

  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
  updateItemRoles() {
    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
      } else {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
      }
    }
  }

  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys
    return Array.from(this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [role="menuitem"]:not(.tw-hidden)'));
  }

  isOpen() {
    return this.trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  }

  open(focus: 'first' | 'last') {
    this.updateItemRoles();
    showElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    const items = this.items();
    (focus === 'first' ? items[0] : items.at(-1))?.focus();
  }

  close(restoreFocus: boolean) {
    // only restore when focus is still in the popup, so focus moved elsewhere by an item handler is kept
    const focusInPopup = this.popup.contains(document.activeElement);
    hideElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
  }

  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
  };

  // a native button fires "click" on Space keyup, which would toggle the menu shut again or double-activate an item
  preventSpaceClick = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault();
  };

  onTriggerKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      this.open('first');
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      this.open('last');
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  onPopupKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    const items = this.items();
    const current = items.indexOf(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (e.key === 'Tab') {
      // focus the trigger and let the default action move on from there
      this.close(true);
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      e.stopPropagation(); // don't also close a surrounding modal
      this.close(true);
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      items[(current + 1) % items.length].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      items.at(current <= 0 ? -1 : current - 1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Home') {
      items[0].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'End') {
      items.at(-1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      if (current < 0) return;
      items[current].click();
    } else if (e.key.length === 1 && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      this.focusByFirstChar(items, current, e.key);
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  focusByFirstChar(items: HTMLElement[], current: number, char: string) {
    const lower = char.toLowerCase();
    for (let i = 1; i <= items.length; i++) {
      const item = items[(current + i) % items.length];
      if (item.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().startsWith(lower)) {
        item.focus();
        return;
      }
    }
  }
});

async function initRepoProjectSortable(): Promise<void> {
  // the HTML layout is: #project-board.board > .project-column .cards > .issue-card
  const mainBoard = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#project-board')!;
  let boardColumns = mainBoard.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.project-column');
  createSortable(mainBoard, {
    group: 'project-column',
    draggable: '.project-column',
    handle: '.project-column-header',
    delayOnTouchOnly: true,
    delay: 500,
    onSort: async () => { // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises
      boardColumns = mainBoard.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.project-column');

      const columnSorting = {
        columns: Array.from(boardColumns, (column, i) => ({
          columnID: parseInt(column.getAttribute('data-id')!),
          sorting: i,
        })),
      };

      try {
        await POST(mainBoard.getAttribute('data-url')!, {
          data: columnSorting,
        });
      } catch (error) {
        console.error(error);
      }
    },
  });

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, randomString, assertNoJsError} from './utils.ts';

test('profile menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page}) => {
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/');
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();

  const menuBox = (await menu.boundingBox())!;
  expect(menuBox.x + menuBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(page.viewportSize()!.width);

  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Sign Out'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  for (const name of ['Starred', 'Subscriptions', 'Settings']) {
    await page.keyboard.press('s');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name})).toBeFocused();
  }
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/user\/settings$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

```text
		})
		if len(points[i].Changes) == 0 {
			points[i].Changes = nil // keep quiet days out of the JSON
		}
	}

	var deadlineDay time.Time
	if m.DeadlineUnix > 0 {
		deadlineDay = startOfDay(int64(m.DeadlineUnix), loc)
		if civilDay(deadlineDay)-civilDay(lastDay) > burndownHorizonDays {
			deadlineDay = time.Time{} // the fixtures' year 9999, say: drawing it would flatten the chart
		} else {
			result.Deadline = deadlineDay.Format(time.DateOnly)
		}
	}

	if from >= 0 && !deadlineDay.IsZero() {
		fromDay := firstDay.AddDate(0, 0, from)
		if points[from].Remaining > 0 && deadlineDay.After(fromDay) {
			result.Ideal = &BurndownIdeal{From: points[from].Date, FromValue: points[from].Remaining, To: result.Deadline}
		}
	}

	switch {
	case points[last].Scope == 0:
		result.Status = BurndownEmpty
	case points[last].Remaining == 0:
		result.Status = BurndownDone
		done := last
		for done > 0 && points[done-1].Remaining == 0 && points[done-1].Scope > 0 {
			done--
		}
		result.CompletedOn = points[done].Date
	case m.IsClosed:
		result.Status = BurndownClosed
	// history counts from the first day with work: days before it hold nothing to burn, and a window
	// reaching back into them would read the work arriving as work growing
	case last-from < burndownMinHistoryDays:
		result.Status = BurndownInsufficientData
	default:
		window := min(burndownWindowDays, last-from)
		rate := float64(points[last-window].Remaining-points[last].Remaining) / float64(window)
		if rate <= 0 {
			result.Status = BurndownNotBurning
			break
		}
		projected := lastDay.AddDate(0, 0, int(math.Ceil(float64(points[last].Remaining)/rate)))
		result.Status = BurndownProjected
		result.Projected = projected.Format(time.DateOnly)
		if !deadlineDay.IsZero() {
			late := int(civilDay(projected) - civilDay(deadlineDay))
			result.DaysLate = &late
		}
	}
	return result

Both branches are cut from `main` at 38f519923c. Don't commit until the spec review comment is on the issue.

## #131: projected finish on the milestones list

Branch: `feat/issue-131-milestone-projection`

### Steps

1. **Map a burndown to a label (service).** In `services/issue/milestone_burndown.go`, or a new `milestone_projection.go` beside it:
   ```go
   type MilestoneProjection struct {
       Status   BurndownStatus // projected or not_burning
       Date     string         // Projected, "YYYY-MM-DD"
       DaysLate *int           // nil when there's no drawable due date
   }
   func NewMilestoneProjection(b *MilestoneBurndown) *MilestoneProjection // nil means show nothing
   ```
   - `projected` → `{Date, DaysLate}`
   - `not_burning` → `{Status}`
   - `empty`, `insufficient_data`, `done`, `closed` → nil (AC3, AC4)
   - Keeping this a pure function makes AC7's unit test trivial.
   - Edge case: a due date more than 365 days out leaves `Deadline == ""` and `DaysLate == nil`, so the row shows the date with no label. That's acceptable. Add a test row for it and a line under Out of Scope.

2. **Share the permission rule (router).** In `routers/web/repo/milestone.go`, move the `BurndownOptions` logic out of `MilestoneBurndownData` (lines ~292-298) into `burndownOptions(ctx, includePulls bool)`. Call it from both handlers, with `includePulls=false` on the list (AC5, AC6). This keeps the chart and the list from drifting apart.

3. **Compute for each open milestone (router).** In `Milestones` (line ~36), after `miles` loads and only when `!isShowClosed`: loop over `miles`, call `issue.GetMilestoneBurndown`, and build `map[int64]*issue.MilestoneProjection` into `ctx.Data["MilestoneProjections"]`. This is Decision 1: at most `setting.UI.IssuePagingNum` (20) milestones per page.

4. **Render it (template).** In `templates/repo/issue/milestones.tmpl`, inside the not-closed branch after the due-date span (around line 75): `{{with index $.MilestoneProjections .ID}}`
   - projected: `{{svg "octicon-graph" 14}}` + "Projected <date>" (use `DateUtils.AbsoluteShort`, like the due date)
   - `DaysLate > 0`: append "· N days late" with `tw-text-red`
   - `DaysLate <= 0`: append "· on track", muted
   - not_burning: "Not burning down" in `tw-text-warning-text`
   - Give it a `data-test-id` or class, like `milestone-projection`, for the tests.

5. **Locale (`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`),** next to `repo.milestones.burndown.*` (around line 2038):
   - `repo.milestones.projection.projected`: "Projected %s"
   - `repo.milestones.projection.days_late`: plural form; copy how the burndown's day counts pluralise (commit ceeebe5c89)
   - `repo.milestones.projection.on_track`
   - `repo.milestones.projection.not_burning`

6. **Tests.**
   - Unit: `TestNewMilestoneProjection`, table-driven, in `services/issue/` (AC7). Rows: late, on track, exactly on the due date, no due date, due date past the horizon, not burning, empty, insufficient data, done, closed.
   - Integration: extend `tests/integration/milestone_burndown_test.go`, reusing its setup and the two permission tests at lines 207 and 225 as patterns.
     - Load `/{owner}/{repo}/milestones` and assert the projection text for a seeded milestone (AC1).
     - Load `?state=closed` and assert there's no projection (AC4).
     - With pull requests or issues turned off, assert the label matches that viewer's `/burndown` JSON (AC5, AC6).
   - Optional e2e: skip it. A server-rendered label is covered by the integration test, and that keeps runtime down.

7. **Gates:** `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `go test -run '^TestNewMilestoneProjection$' ./services/issue/`, `go test -run '^TestMilestoneBurndown' ./tests/integration/` (check `.claude-students/docs/testing.md` for the DB setup), `make lint-templates`.

### Suggested commits
1. `feat(milestone): map a burndown to a list projection (#131)`: service, plus its unit test
2. `feat(milestone): show projected finish on the milestones list (#131)`: router, template, locale
3. `test(milestone): cover the milestones list projection and its permissions (#131)`

### Size
About 150 lines of Go and template, plus tests. Roughly 2–3 hours with the tests.

## #109: "…" row menus moved to `<aria-menu>`

Branch: `feat/issue-109-aria-menu-row-menus`

Reference implementation: `templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl`, the comment menu migrated in #62. It uses `<aria-menu placement="bottom-end" pointing>`, then a `<button type="button" class="btn interact-fg" aria-label="…">`, then `<div class="menu">` with `.item` children.

### Steps

1. **Support disabled items in `<aria-menu>` (Decision 2, AC4).** In `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`:
   - `updateItemRoles()`: on `.item`, set or remove `aria-disabled="true"` from `classList.contains('disabled')`.
   - `onPopupKeyDown`, Enter/Space branch: if the current item is `aria-disabled`, `preventDefault` and return without clicking.
   - Popup `click` listener: if the clicked menuitem is `aria-disabled`, `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()` and return. The menu stays open, and the delegated `link-action` handler can't fire.
   - `items()` stays as it is, so disabled items are still reachable with the arrow keys.
   - Check that `.disabled` styling still applies outside Fomantic. If it doesn't, add a rule to the existing aria-menu CSS (`web_src/css/`, search for `aria-menu`).

Keep the `disabled` / `link-action` and `show-modal` attributes exactly as they are.

3. **Run row menus (AC1): `templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl:55-73`.** Same shape, with `placement="bottom-end"` (this answers the spec's open question). Keep `flex-items-menu` on `.menu` if it still styles the icon gap.

```markdown
## User Story

As a maintainer tracking several milestones, I want the milestones list to show each open milestone's projected finish, so that I can see which milestones are slipping without opening each burndown chart (#14).

## User Scenario

A maintainer opens a repository's Milestones tab, where three milestones are open. Under "Sprint 3" they see "Projected to finish on Nov 12, 4 days after the due date" in red next to the due date. "Docs refresh" reads "Projected to finish on Nov 2, the due date". "Backlog" has no due date, and reads "Projected to finish on Dec 1". A fourth milestone, opened yesterday, shows nothing because there isn't enough history yet. They click "Sprint 3", and its burndown chart shows the same sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open milestone with a due date whose burndown status is `projected`, when the Milestones tab renders, then its row shows the chart's own projection sentence (`repo.milestones.burndown.projected_late_1`/`_n`, `projected_on_due_date` or `projected_on_time_1`/`_n`). A projection after the due date is shown in red. One on or before the due date is muted.
- [ ] AC2: Given an open milestone with no due date (or one too far out for the chart to draw) whose status is `projected`, when the list renders, then its row shows `repo.milestones.burndown.projected` with the date, muted.
- [ ] AC3: Given an open milestone whose status is `not_burning`, when the list renders, then its row shows `repo.milestones.burndown.status_not_burning` in the warning colour. Any other status shows nothing new.
- [ ] AC4: Given a closed milestone, when the closed tab renders, then its row shows no projection.
- [ ] AC5: Given any open milestone, when the list renders, then its projection sentence is the one that milestone's chart shows by default (issues, or pull requests for a viewer who can read only pull requests).
- [ ] AC6: Given a viewer who can read issues but not pull requests (or the reverse), when the list renders, then the projection counts only the kind they can read, as the chart does.
- [ ] AC7: A table-driven Go unit test covers every status-to-sentence case: late (1 day and N days), on the due date, early (1 day and N days), no due date, a due date beyond the chart's horizon, not burning, and each status that shows nothing. An integration test covers the list page:
  - (a) a milestone whose `created_unix` and milestone/close comment timestamps are backdated in the DB, so that it reaches `projected` and its row text matches its `/burndown` JSON (AC1, AC5)
  - (b) a new milestone (`insufficient_data`) that shows nothing
  - (c) the closed tab (AC4)
  - (d) the two permission cases (AC6)

  The existing burndown tests still pass.

## Out of Scope

- Sorting or filtering the list by projected finish.
- The cross-repository milestones dashboard (`/milestones`).
- An "include pull requests" toggle on the list: the list uses the chart's default kind.
- Caching or storing projections. See Decision 1.
- Matching the row's progress bar. The bar and its open/closed counts come from `num_issues`, which counts issues and pull requests together (`UpdateMilestoneCounters`). The projection counts the chart's default kind, issues for most viewers. A milestone of mostly pull requests can show a high percentage next to "Not enough progress…". That is expected, not a bug.

## Open Questions

- None. (Resolved in review: "on time" and "on the due date" stay muted, because "N days after the due date" carries its meaning in the text, so red isn't the only signal. Projections are computed only for open milestones on the current page, per Decision 1.)

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: where the projection is computed

**Decision:** Compute it on the server in the `Milestones` handler, calling the existing `issue.GetMilestoneBurndown` for each open milestone on the current page, and render it in `templates/repo/issue/milestones.tmpl`. The choice between issues and pull requests, now inline in `MilestoneBurndownData`, moves into one helper that both handlers call.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Fetch each row's projection in the browser from the existing `/milestone/{id}/burndown` JSON endpoint.
- (b) Store the projected finish in a new `milestone` column, recomputed whenever an issue opens, closes or changes milestone.

**Rationale:** (a) costs one HTTP request per row, makes the rows shift as results arrive, and shows nothing without JavaScript. (b) needs a migration and hooks on every issue state and milestone change, and a stored projection goes stale as days pass with no events, because the burn rate is measured over a moving 14-day window. Server-side reuse, with the shared helper, keeps one source of truth, so AC5 and AC6 hold by construction.

**Consequences:** Easier: no new endpoint, migration or JavaScript, and the list can never disagree with the chart. Harder: each open milestone costs at least 3 queries (scope events, items, state events). The page size (`setting.UI.IssuePagingNum`) defaults to 20, so that is up to 60 extra queries per page load. Each query reads the milestone's whole history, so a long-lived "Backlog" milestone costs the most. If the list gets slow, a batched query or a cache is the follow-up.

### Decision 2: what the row shows

**Decision:** Show the chart's own projection sentence as a text label, reusing the `repo.milestones.burndown.*` locale keys (including their `_1`/`_n` singular and plural pairs). The date is rendered with `DateUtils.AbsoluteShort` like the due date beside it, and a far-off projection is shown as-is, as the chart shows it.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A small sparkline of the burndown in each row.
- (b) An on/off-track badge from comparing remaining work to the ideal line today.

**Rationale:** (a) is unreadable at row size, adds a chart library to the list page, and gives a screen reader nothing useful without extra text. (b) can say "off track" while the projection says it will finish on time, because the ideal line and the projection measure different things. The chart page would then contradict the list. Reusing the chart's sentences means the two pages can't word the same fact differently, and it adds no new strings to translate.

**Consequences:** Easier: the label is plain text, so it's accessible and testable with an HTML assertion. Harder: the list doesn't show the trend's shape, so users open the milestone for that. The sentence is longer than a short badge, so it may wrap on narrow screens.

## Scope

medium

// Copyright 2018 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package repo

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"

	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/renderhelper"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/modules/markup/markdown"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/templates"
	"gitea.dev/modules/web"
	"gitea.dev/routers/common"
	"gitea.dev/routers/web/feed"
	shared_issue "gitea.dev/routers/web/shared/issue"
	"gitea.dev/services/context"
	"gitea.dev/services/forms"
	"gitea.dev/services/issue"

	"xorm.io/builder"
)

const (
	tplMilestone       templates.TplName = "repo/issue/milestones"
	tplMilestoneNew    templates.TplName = "repo/issue/milestone_new"
	tplMilestoneIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/milestone_issues"
)

			return
		}

		ctx.ServerError("GetMilestoneByID", err)
		return
	}

	rctx := renderhelper.NewRenderContextRepoComment(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository)
	milestone.RenderedContent, err = markdown.RenderString(rctx, milestone.Content)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("RenderString", err)
		return
	}

	ctx.Data["Title"] = milestone.Name
	ctx.Data["Milestone"] = milestone
	ctx.PageData["milestoneBurndownLink"] = fmt.Sprintf("%s/milestone/%d/burndown", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, milestone.ID)
	ctx.PageData["repoLink"] = ctx.Repo.RepoLink // the chart links each changed item

	prepareIssueFilterAndList(ctx, milestoneID, projectIDs, optional.None[bool](), shared_issue.DueDateFilter{}) // the due date filter is only offered on the issue and pull request lists

	ret := issue.ParseTemplatesFromDefaultBranch(ctx.Repo.Repository, ctx.Repo.GitRepo)
	ctx.Data["NewIssueChooseTemplate"] = len(ret.IssueTemplates) > 0

	ctx.Data["CanWriteIssues"] = ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWriteIssuesOrPulls(false)
	ctx.Data["CanWritePulls"] = ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWriteIssuesOrPulls(true)

	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplMilestoneIssues)
}

// MilestoneBurndownData returns the milestone's burndown as JSON for the chart on its page
func MilestoneBurndownData(ctx *context.Context) {
	milestone, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneByRepoID(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID, ctx.PathParamInt64("id"))
	if err != nil {
		if issues_model.IsErrMilestoneNotExist(err) {
			ctx.NotFound(err)
			return
		}
		ctx.ServerError("GetMilestoneByRepoID", err)
		return
	}

	// issues by default, pull requests on request, and neither kind unless the viewer may read it: the route
	// lets in a reader of either, and the chart must not count or list the other. A reader of pull requests
	// only gets them by default, or their chart would always claim the milestone is empty.
	canReadIssues := ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypeIssues)
	burndown, err := issue.GetMilestoneBurndown(ctx, milestone, issue.BurndownOptions{
		Issues: canReadIssues,
		Pulls:  ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypePullRequests) && (ctx.FormBool("include_pulls") || !canReadIssues),
	})
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetMilestoneBurndown", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, burndown)
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	unit_model "gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMilestoneBurndown(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	t.Run("Data", func(t *testing.T) {
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)

		due := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, 7)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{
			Title: "burndown", Deadline: &due,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		milestone := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Milestone{})

		indexes := make([]int64, 0, 2)
		for _, title := range []string{"first", "second"} {
			req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
				Title: title, Milestone: milestone.ID,
			}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			indexes = append(indexes, DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Issue{}).Index)
		}
		closed := "closed"
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", indexes[0]), api.EditIssueOption{
			State: &closed,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)

		// anyone who can read the repository's issues can read its burndown
		req = NewRequest(t, "GET", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestone.ID))
		burndown := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})

		// one day of history, or two if the test ran across midnight; too few to project either way
		require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
		require.LessOrEqual(t, len(burndown.Points), 2)
		today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownInsufficientData, burndown.Status)
		require.NotNil(t, burndown.Ideal)
		assert.Equal(t, burndown.Points[0].Date, burndown.Ideal.From)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, burndown.Ideal.FromValue)
		assert.Equal(t, burndown.Deadline, burndown.Ideal.To)

		// the chart and the progress bar above it must count the same thing
		row := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Milestone{ID: milestone.ID})
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues-row.NumClosedIssues, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues, today.Scope)
	})

	t.Run("RealLifecycle", func(t *testing.T) {
		// close, reopen and move through the API, so the history the chart replays is written by the
		// real code paths rather than built by hand as in the unit tests
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
		createMilestone := func(title string) int64 {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{Title: title}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			return DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Milestone{}).ID
		}
		sprint, other := createMilestone("sprint"), createMilestone("other")

		issues := map[string]*api.Issue{}
		for _, title := range []string{"closed", "reopened", "moved", "open"} {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{Title: title, Milestone: sprint}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			issues[title] = DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Issue{})
		}
		edit := func(title string, option api.EditIssueOption) {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", issues[title].Index), option).AddTokenAuth(token)
			MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
		}
		closed, open := "closed", "open"

export type LinePoint = {x: string, y: number};

export type MarkerPoint = LinePoint & {count: number};

// fills %s and %d in order, the way the server-side locale strings are written
export function formatLocale(template: string, ...args: Array<string | number>): string {
  let next = 0;
  return template.replace(/%[sd]/g, () => String(args[next++]));
}

// the one-line verdict above the chart; it carries the late or early state in words, not only in colour
export function burndownSummary(data: MilestoneBurndown, locale: BurndownSummaryLocale): string {
  switch (data.status) {
    case 'done':
      return formatLocale(locale.statusDone, data.completedOn);
    case 'closed':
      return locale.statusClosed;
    case 'not_burning':
      return locale.statusNotBurning;
    case 'insufficient_data':
      return locale.statusInsufficient;
    case 'projected':
      if (data.daysLate === null) return formatLocale(locale.projected, data.projected);
      if (data.daysLate === 0) return formatLocale(locale.projectedOnDueDate, data.projected);
      if (data.daysLate > 0) {
        return formatLocale(data.daysLate === 1 ? locale.projectedLateOne : locale.projectedLate, data.projected, data.daysLate);
      }
      return formatLocale(data.daysLate === -1 ? locale.projectedOnTimeOne : locale.projectedOnTime, data.projected, -data.daysLate);
    default:
      return '';
  }
}

export function idealLine(data: MilestoneBurndown): LinePoint[] {
  if (!data.ideal) return [];
  return [{x: data.ideal.from, y: data.ideal.fromValue}, {x: data.ideal.to, y: 0}];
}

// from today's remaining work down to zero on the projected day
const dayMillis = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const projectionHorizonDays = 365; // as far past the chart as the server draws a due date

// a slow burn can project years ahead; drawing that would squash the history into a sliver, so the
// summary still states the date but the chart does not stretch to it
export function projectionOnChart(data: MilestoneBurndown): boolean {
  if (data.status !== 'projected' || data.points.length === 0) return false;
  const today = Date.parse(data.points[data.points.length - 1].date); // both parse as UTC midnight
  return Date.parse(data.projected) - today <= projectionHorizonDays * dayMillis;
}

export function projectionLine(data: MilestoneBurndown): LinePoint[] {
  if (!projectionOnChart(data)) return [];
  const today = data.points[data.points.length - 1];
  return [{x: today.date, y: today.remaining}, {x: data.projected, y: 0}];
}

// ParseLegacy parses the datetime in legacy format, eg: "2016-01-02" in server's timezone.
// It shouldn't be used in new code. New code should use Time or TimeStamp as much as possible.
func (du *DateUtils) ParseLegacy(datetime string) time.Time {
	return parseLegacy(datetime)
}

func parseLegacy(datetime string) time.Time {
	t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, datetime)
	if err != nil {
		t, _ = time.ParseInLocation(time.DateOnly, datetime, setting.DefaultUILocation)
	}
	return t
}

func anyToTime(value any) (t time.Time, isZero bool) {
	switch v := value.(type) {
	case nil:
		// it is zero
	case *time.Time:
		if v != nil {
			t = *v
		}
	case time.Time:
		t = v
	case timeutil.TimeStamp:
		t = v.AsTime()
	case timeutil.TimeStampNano:
		t = v.AsTime()
	case int:
		t = timeutil.TimeStamp(v).AsTime()
	case int64:
		t = timeutil.TimeStamp(v).AsTime()
	default:
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("Unsupported time type %T", value))
	}
	return t, t.IsZero() || t.Unix() == 0
}

func dateTimeFormat(format string, datetime any) template.HTML {
	t, isZero := anyToTime(datetime)
	if isZero {
		return "-"
	}
	var textEscaped string
	datetimeEscaped := html.EscapeString(t.Format(time.RFC3339))
	if format == "full" {
		textEscaped = html.EscapeString(t.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -07:00"))
	} else {
		textEscaped = html.EscapeString(t.Format("2006-01-02"))
	}

	attrs := []string{`weekday=""`, `year="numeric"`}
	switch format {
	case "short", "long": // date only
		attrs = append(attrs, `threshold="P0Y"`, `month="`+format+`"`, `day="numeric"`, `prefix=""`)
	case "full": // full date including time
		attrs = append(attrs, `format="datetime"`, `month="short"`, `day="numeric"`, `hour="numeric"`, `minute="numeric"`, `second="numeric"`, `data-tooltip-content`, `data-tooltip-interactive="true"`)
	default:
		panic("Unsupported format " + format)
	}

	return template.HTML(fmt.Sprintf(`<relative-time %s datetime="%s">%s</relative-time>`, strings.Join(attrs, " "), datetimeEscaped, textEscaped))
}

func timeSinceTo(then any, now time.Time) template.HTML {
	thenTime, isZero := anyToTime(then)
	if isZero {
		return "-"
	}

	friendlyText := thenTime.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -07:00")

	// document: https://github.com/github/relative-time-element
	attrs := `tense="past"`
	isFuture := now.Before(thenTime)
	if isFuture {
		attrs = `tense="future"`
	}

	// declare data-tooltip-content attribute to switch from "title" tooltip to "tippy" tooltip
	htm := fmt.Sprintf(`<relative-time prefix="" %s datetime="%s" data-tooltip-content data-tooltip-interactive="true">%s</relative-time>`,
		attrs, thenTime.Format(time.RFC3339), friendlyText)
	return template.HTML(htm)
}

	var c int64

	}

	ruleFunc, ok := trNLangRules[l.Lang]
	if !ok {
		ruleFunc = trNLangRules["en-US"]
	}

	if ruleFunc(c) == 0 {
		return l.Tr(key1, args...)
	}
	return l.Tr(keyN, args...)
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issue

const burndownLocalePrefix = "repo.milestones.burndown."

// MilestoneProjection is the one-line verdict a milestone list row shows. It reuses the chart summary's
// locale keys, so the list and the chart can't word the same projection differently.
type MilestoneProjection struct {
	Key1       string // the singular key; the same as KeyN when the sentence has no day count
	KeyN       string
	Date       string // the projected finish, "YYYY-MM-DD"; empty when the sentence names no date
	Days       int    // days after or before the due date, set only when WithDays
	WithDays   bool   // the sentence takes a day count after the date
	Late       bool
	NotBurning bool
}

// NewMilestoneProjection picks the chart summary's sentence for a burndown, mirroring burndownSummary in
// web_src/js/components/RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.ts. It returns nil for a status the list leaves out.
func NewMilestoneProjection(b *MilestoneBurndown) *MilestoneProjection {
	switch b.Status {
	case BurndownNotBurning:
		return &MilestoneProjection{Key1: burndownLocalePrefix + "status_not_burning", KeyN: burndownLocalePrefix + "status_not_burning", NotBurning: true}
	case BurndownProjected:
		p := &MilestoneProjection{Date: b.Projected}
		switch {
		case b.DaysLate == nil: // no due date, or one too far out to draw
			p.Key1, p.KeyN = burndownLocalePrefix+"projected", burndownLocalePrefix+"projected"
		case *b.DaysLate == 0:
			p.Key1, p.KeyN = burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_on_due_date", burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_on_due_date"
		case *b.DaysLate > 0:
			p.Key1, p.KeyN = burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_late_1", burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_late_n"
			p.Days, p.WithDays, p.Late = *b.DaysLate, true, true
		default:
			p.Key1, p.KeyN = burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_on_time_1", burndownLocalePrefix+"projected_on_time_n"
			p.Days, p.WithDays = -*b.DaysLate, true
		}
		return p
	}
	return nil
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issue

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestNewMilestoneProjection(t *testing.T) {
	days := func(n int) *int { return &n }
	projected := func(daysLate *int) *MilestoneBurndown {
		return &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownProjected, Projected: "2026-11-12", DaysLate: daysLate}
	}
	key := func(name string) string { return burndownLocalePrefix + name }

	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		burndown *MilestoneBurndown
		want     *MilestoneProjection
	}{
		{"LateOneDay", projected(days(1)), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected_late_1"), KeyN: key("projected_late_n"), Date: "2026-11-12", Days: 1, WithDays: true, Late: true,
		}},
		{"LateDays", projected(days(4)), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected_late_1"), KeyN: key("projected_late_n"), Date: "2026-11-12", Days: 4, WithDays: true, Late: true,
		}},
		{"OnDueDate", projected(days(0)), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected_on_due_date"), KeyN: key("projected_on_due_date"), Date: "2026-11-12",
		}},
		{"EarlyOneDay", projected(days(-1)), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected_on_time_1"), KeyN: key("projected_on_time_n"), Date: "2026-11-12", Days: 1, WithDays: true,
		}},
		{"EarlyDays", projected(days(-6)), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected_on_time_1"), KeyN: key("projected_on_time_n"), Date: "2026-11-12", Days: 6, WithDays: true,
		}},
		// also what the burndown reports for a due date past the chart's horizon
		{"NoDueDate", projected(nil), &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("projected"), KeyN: key("projected"), Date: "2026-11-12",
		}},
		{"NotBurning", &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownNotBurning}, &MilestoneProjection{
			Key1: key("status_not_burning"), KeyN: key("status_not_burning"), NotBurning: true,
		}},
		{"Empty", &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownEmpty}, nil},
		{"InsufficientData", &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownInsufficientData}, nil},
		{"Done", &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownDone, CompletedOn: "2026-11-01"}, nil},
		{"Closed", &MilestoneBurndown{Status: BurndownClosed}, nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, c.want, NewMilestoneProjection(c.burndown))
		})
	}
}

func replayMilestoneItem(item issues_model.MilestoneItem, events []issues_model.MilestoneEvent, milestoneID, milestoneCreated int64) []burndownDelta {
	events = slices.Clone(events) // synthetic events are appended below
	created := int64(item.CreatedUnix)
	var firstScope *issues_model.MilestoneEvent
	hasClose := false
	for i := range events {
		switch events[i].Type {
		case issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone:
			if firstScope == nil {
				firstScope = &events[i]
			}
		case issues_model.CommentTypeClose, issues_model.CommentTypeMergePull:
			hasClose = true
		}
	}

	// synthetic events take id 0 so they sort before a real comment in the same second
	joinAt := max(created, milestoneCreated)
	if firstScope == nil && item.MilestoneID == milestoneID {
		events = append(events, issues_model.MilestoneEvent{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone, MilestoneID: milestoneID, CreatedUnix: timeutil.TimeStamp(joinAt)})
	} else if firstScope != nil && firstScope.MilestoneID != milestoneID {
		// its first recorded move is out of the milestone, so it was in it before then
		joinAt = min(joinAt, int64(firstScope.CreatedUnix))
		events = append(events, issues_model.MilestoneEvent{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone, MilestoneID: milestoneID, CreatedUnix: timeutil.TimeStamp(joinAt)})
	}
	if item.IsClosed && !hasClose {

// milestoneWithClosedIssue adds a closed issue to milestone 1 of user2/repo1, which already holds
// pull request #2, so the chart has one item of each kind and the issue appears in today's changes
func milestoneWithClosedIssue(t *testing.T) *api.Issue {
	token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, loginUser(t, "user2"), auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
	req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
		Title: "only for issue readers", Milestone: 1,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	created := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Issue{})
	closed := "closed"
	req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", created.Index), api.EditIssueOption{
		State: &closed,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
	return created
}

func readBurndown(t *testing.T, url string) *issue_service.MilestoneBurndown {
	return DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusOK), &issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})
}

func TestMilestoneBurndownWithoutPullAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	created := milestoneWithClosedIssue(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypePullRequests}))

	// asking for pull requests cannot count one the viewer may not read
	burndown := readBurndown(t, "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown?include_pulls=1")
	require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
	today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
	assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope, "the issue only")
	for _, c := range today.Changes {
		assert.False(t, c.IsPull)
	}
	require.Len(t, today.Changes, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, created.Index, today.Changes[0].Index)
}

func TestMilestoneBurndownWithoutIssueAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	created := milestoneWithClosedIssue(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypeIssues}))

	// a pull request reader still reaches the milestone and sees its pull requests by default, rather
	// than an "empty" chart; the closed issue is never counted or listed, asked for or not
	for _, url := range []string{"/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown", "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown?include_pulls=1"} {
		burndown := readBurndown(t, url)
		require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points, url)
		today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope, "the pull request only: %s", url)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining, url)
		for _, p := range burndown.Points {
			for _, c := range p.Changes {
				assert.NotEqual(t, created.Index, c.Index, "an unreadable issue leaked into %s of %s", p.Date, url)
			}
		}
	}
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	unit_model "gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"

// backdatedMilestone creates a milestone in user2/repo1, due today, whose three issues joined six days ago
// and two of which closed four and two days ago. API-created history is all from today, too little to
// project, so the timestamps are moved back in the database.
func backdatedMilestone(t *testing.T) int64 {
	token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, loginUser(t, "user2"), auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
	due := time.Now()
	req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{
		Title: "projected", Deadline: &due,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	milestoneID := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Milestone{}).ID

	ids := make([]int64, 0, 3)
	indexes := make([]int64, 0, 3)
	for _, title := range []string{"closed first", "closed second", "still open"} {
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
			Title: title, Milestone: milestoneID,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		created := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Issue{})
		ids = append(ids, created.ID)
		indexes = append(indexes, created.Index)
	}
	closed := "closed"
	for _, index := range indexes[:2] {
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", index), api.EditIssueOption{
			State: &closed,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
	}

	daysAgo := func(n int) int64 { return time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, -n).Unix() }
	exec := func(query string, args ...any) {
		_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).Exec(append([]any{query}, args...)...)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	exec("UPDATE milestone SET created_unix=? WHERE id=?", daysAgo(6), milestoneID)
	for i, id := range ids {
		exec("UPDATE issue SET created_unix=? WHERE id=?", daysAgo(6), id)
		exec("UPDATE comment SET created_unix=? WHERE issue_id=? AND type=?", daysAgo(6), id, issues_model.CommentTypeMilestone)
		if i < 2 {
			closedAt := daysAgo(4 - 2*i)
			exec("UPDATE issue SET closed_unix=? WHERE id=?", closedAt, id)
			exec("UPDATE comment SET created_unix=? WHERE issue_id=? AND type=?", closedAt, id, issues_model.CommentTypeClose)
		}
	}
	return milestoneID
}

func milestoneRow(t *testing.T, url string, milestoneID int64) *goquery.Selection {
	doc := NewHTMLParser(t, MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusOK).Body)
	row := doc.Find(".milestone-list > .item").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool {
		return s.Find(fmt.Sprintf(`a[href$="/milestone/%d"]`, milestoneID)).Length() > 0
	})
	require.Equal(t, 1, row.Length(), "milestone %d on %s", milestoneID, url)
	return row
}

func TestMilestoneListProjection(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	milestoneID := backdatedMilestone(t)

	t.Run("Projected", func(t *testing.T) {
		// the list must say what the chart says
		burndown := readBurndown(t, fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestoneID))
		require.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownProjected, burndown.Status)
		require.NotNil(t, burndown.DaysLate)
		require.Positive(t, *burndown.DaysLate, "due today, so any projection is late")

		projection := milestoneRow(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones", milestoneID).Find(".milestone-projection")
		require.Equal(t, 1, projection.Length())
		assert.True(t, projection.HasClass("tw-text-red"))
		datetime, _ := projection.Find("relative-time").Attr("datetime")
		assert.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(datetime, burndown.Projected), "%q starts with %q", datetime, burndown.Projected)
		want := fmt.Sprintf("%d days after the due date", *burndown.DaysLate)
		if *burndown.DaysLate == 1 {
			want = "1 day after the due date"
		}
		assert.Contains(t, projection.Text(), want)
	})

	t.Run("InsufficientData", func(t *testing.T) {
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, loginUser(t, "user2"), auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{Title: "new"}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		newID := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &api.Milestone{}).ID
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{Title: "today", Milestone: newID}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)

		assert.Equal(t, 0, milestoneRow(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones", newID).Find(".milestone-projection").Length())
	})

	t.Run("ClosedTab", func(t *testing.T) {
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, loginUser(t, "user2"), auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
		closed := "closed"
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones/%d", milestoneID), api.EditMilestoneOption{
			State: &closed,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)

		assert.Equal(t, 0, milestoneRow(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones?state=closed", milestoneID).Find(".milestone-projection").Length())
	})
}

func TestMilestoneListProjectionWithoutPullAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	milestoneID := backdatedMilestone(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypePullRequests}))

	// the milestone holds issues only, so an issue reader still gets its projection
	assert.Equal(t, 1, milestoneRow(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones", milestoneID).Find(".milestone-projection").Length())
}

func TestMilestoneListProjectionWithoutIssueAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	milestoneID := backdatedMilestone(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypeIssues}))

	// a pull request reader counts pull requests only, of which the milestone has none, so the
	// issues' projection must not show
	burndown := readBurndown(t, fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestoneID))
	assert.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownEmpty, burndown.Status)
	assert.Equal(t, 0, milestoneRow(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones", milestoneID).Find(".milestone-projection").Length())
}

## Conventions & invariants

- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

```markdown
Closes #131

## What changed

Each open milestone on a repository's Milestones tab now shows its projected finish, worded exactly like the burndown chart's summary on the milestone page. For example: "Projected to finish on Nov 12, 4 days after the due date" in red, "…, the due date" or "…, 3 days before the due date" muted, or "Not enough progress to project a finish date" in the warning colour. Milestones with too little history, done milestones and the closed tab show nothing new.

- `services/issue/milestone_projection.go`: `NewMilestoneProjection` maps a `MilestoneBurndown` to the chart's existing `repo.milestones.burndown.*` locale keys (singular/plural pair, date, day count, tone). It mirrors `burndownSummary` in `RepoMilestoneBurndown.utils.ts`.
- `routers/web/repo/milestone.go`: the choice between issues and pull requests moves out of `MilestoneBurndownData` into a shared `burndownOptions` helper. `Milestones` calls `GetMilestoneBurndown` for each open milestone on the current page.
- `templates/repo/issue/milestones.tmpl`: renders the sentence after the due date, with the date through `DateUtils.AbsoluteShort` like the due date beside it.

No new locale keys, endpoint, migration or JavaScript.

## Why

Before this, seeing whether a milestone was slipping meant opening each milestone's chart. This covers the acceptance criteria in #131:

- **AC1:** late, on the due date, and early sentences, with singular and plural day counts; red only when late.
- **AC2:** no due date, or one past the chart's horizon, gives the plain "Projected to finish on %s".
- **AC3:** `not_burning` shows the warning sentence. Every other status shows nothing.
- **AC4:** the closed tab computes and shows nothing.
- **AC5 and AC6:** the list and the chart share `burndownOptions` and the same burndown, so they count the same kinds and say the same thing.
- **AC7:** see below.

## How it was tested

- **Unit:** `TestNewMilestoneProjection` (`services/issue/milestone_projection_test.go`) is a table-driven test of every status-to-sentence case: late 1 day / N days, on the due date, early 1 day / N days, no due date (also the beyond-horizon case), not burning, and empty, insufficient data, done and closed returning nil. The sentence choice is pure logic, so this is where the edge cases live.
- **Integration:** `tests/integration/milestone_list_projection_test.go`. History created through the API is all from today, too little to project, so `backdatedMilestone` creates a milestone due today with three issues through the API, then moves the milestone, issue and comment timestamps back 6, 4 and 2 days in the DB. That gives a real `projected` burndown.
  - `Projected` (AC1, AC5): the row's sentence is red, its `<relative-time>` carries the same date as the `/burndown` JSON, and its day count matches the JSON's `daysLate`.
  - `InsufficientData`: a milestone created today shows nothing.
  - `ClosedTab` (AC4): after closing the milestone, its row on `?state=closed` has no projection.
  - `WithoutPullAccess` / `WithoutIssueAccess` (AC6): with pull requests turned off, the issue-only milestone still projects. With issues turned off, the pull-request reader's burndown is `empty` and the row shows nothing.
- I confirmed `WithoutIssueAccess` fails when the list counts both kinds regardless of permission, so the test does guard the permission check.
- The existing `TestMilestoneBurndown*` integration tests still pass after the `burndownOptions` refactor.

## CI / manual verification

Run locally on this branch (SQLite):

- `go test -run '^TestNewMilestoneProjection$' ./services/issue/`: ok
- `go test -tags 'sqlite sqlite_unlock_notify' -run '^(TestMilestoneListProjection.*|TestMilestoneBurndown.*)$' gitea.dev/tests/integration`: ok (6 new tests and subtests, plus the existing burndown tests)
- `golangci-lint run` on `./services/issue/... ./routers/web/repo/... ./tests/integration/...`: 0 issues
- `make lint-templates`: 0 errors
- `make fmt`: no changes

## Design

As in the issue's Design Decisions. Decision 1: computed on the server per open milestone on the page, with the shared `burndownOptions` helper. Decision 2: reuse the chart's own sentences. No change during implementation.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- The sentence choice now exists twice: in Go (`NewMilestoneProjection`) and in TypeScript (`burndownSummary`). Each cross-references the other in a comment, but a new status or wording has to change both. Moving the chart's summary to the server would remove the copy, but it would change #14's chart and is out of scope here.
- The list costs at least 3 queries per open milestone on the page: up to 60 per load at the default page size of 20, each reading that milestone's full history. That was accepted in Decision 1. A batched query or a cache is the follow-up if the list gets slow.
- The integration test backdates history with raw `UPDATE` statements on `milestone`, `issue` and `comment`. That couples the test to column names, the same way `actions_job_test.go` does.

**Encountered:**
- The row's progress bar and open/closed counts come from `num_issues`, which counts issues and pull requests together. The projection counts the chart's default kind (issues for most viewers), so the two can differ on a milestone of mostly pull requests. I left it alone and documented it in the issue's Out of Scope, following the spec review.
- The chart's summary wording lived only in the frontend, so the list couldn't reuse it directly. See the duplication above.

import './aria-menu.ts';

// tests touch document.activeElement, so they must stay synchronous to be safe under concurrent sequencing
function renderMenu(labels: string[] = ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry', 'Blueberry']) {
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <aria-menu>
      <button type="button">Fruit</button>
      <div class="menu">
        ${labels.map((label) => `<div class="item">${label}</div>`).join('')}
        <div class="divider"></div>
        <a class="item" href="#">Settings</a>
      </div>
    </aria-menu>
    <button type="button" class="after">after</button>
  `;
  document.body.append(root);
  const menu = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('aria-menu')!;
  const trigger = menu.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(':scope > button')!;
  const popup = menu.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.menu')!;
  const items = Array.from(popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.item'));
  return {root, menu, trigger, popup, items, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

function isOpen(trigger: HTMLElement, popup: HTMLElement) {
  return trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true' && !popup.classList.contains('tw-hidden');
}

describe('AC5 ARIA attributes', () => {
  test('trigger and popup carry the menu button roles', () => {
    const {trigger, popup, items, cleanup} = renderMenu();
    expect(trigger.getAttribute('aria-haspopup')).toBe('menu');
    expect(trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');
    expect(popup.id).not.toBe('');
    expect(trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls')).toBe(popup.id);
    expect(popup.getAttribute('role')).toBe('menu');
    for (const item of items) {
      expect(item.getAttribute('role')).toBe('menuitem');
      expect(item.getAttribute('tabindex')).toBe('-1');
    }
    expect(popup.querySelector('.divider')!.getAttribute('role')).toBe('separator');
    expect(popup.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
    cleanup();
  });

  test('aria-expanded follows the open state', () => {
    const {trigger, popup, cleanup} = renderMenu();
    trigger.click();
    expect(isOpen(trigger, popup)).toBe(true);
    trigger.click();
    expect(isOpen(trigger, popup)).toBe(false);
    cleanup();
  });

  test('the popup is named by its trigger unless it already has a name', () => {
    const {trigger, popup, cleanup} = renderMenu();
    expect(trigger.id).not.toBe('');
    expect(popup.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')).toBe(trigger.id);
    cleanup();
